newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Progressive in breach of loan requirement.
newsitem.headline: Progressive in breach of loan requirement.

text.p: Progressive Enterprises' plunge in profit in the July year has left it in breach of the conditions of its bank loans.
Under the supermarket operator's banking covenants, earnings before interest and tax needed to be at least two times its annual interest charge.
However, a decline in those earnings to $22.87 million, down from $44.58 million the previous year, fell well short of the required cover on its interest bill of $17.18 million.
Managing director Graeme Kelly said the banks had given the company 12 months to fix the imbalance.
Alternative bankers had not been sought because no problem was envisaged.
"Given the sort of interest bill, the earnings before interest and tax is clearly not that difficult to achieve if you take out the Georgie Pie problem," he said.

With the programme of reducing debt -- term debt fell by $29.6 million to $180.9 million in the year to July -- Kelly expected that an earnings level of around $30 million should be sufficient to cover interest charges in the current year.
The Georgie Pie fast food outlet wiped around $8.5 million from the group's earnings in the latest financial year.
But Kelly was confident that that problem had been arrested by a conditional agreement with McDonald's for 17 of Georgie Pie's 32 sites.

The remaining sites would be profitable for the group. But Kelly indicated there was no shortage of potential buyers, as a number of overseas fast food chains were looking to enter the New Zealand market.
Kelly played down talk of problems with the sales process to McDonald's.
While there was always the possibility that something would come up, "at this point in the process no one has come to me to say they are not transferring," he said.
Four of the 17 sites were operated under franchise arrangements. All four had been offered the opportunity to take on a McDonald's franchise.
The other 13 sites were owned by the group, although some sites were leased.
McDonald's had only wanted 12 of the Georgie Pie sites, Kelly said. But after lengthy negotiations it had agreed to take 17.
